proofs.full_local_argument: This is a local reconstruction, not a quotation or a claim that the source supplies these justifications. Write a=l_f1, b=l_g1, c=l_f0, k=l_g2 and mu=mu_g. Gradients are columns. (1) Existence and regularity. Integrating the a-Lipschitz gradient of f along any y-segment gives f(x,z)>=f(x,y)+<f_y(x,y),z-y>-(a/2)||z-y||^2. Combining with strong convexity of g shows L_lambda(x,.) is m-strongly convex, where m=lambda mu-a>=lambda mu/2>0. Its quadratic lower bound implies coercivity, hence existence and uniqueness of v; the same argument for g gives u. Since g is C2 and H=D_y g_y(x,u) is positive definite with H>=mu I, the implicit function theorem applied to g_y(x,u)=0 gives local C1 dependence of u, and uniqueness patches these maps globally. Put B=D_y g_x(x,u), an x-by-y matrix. Symmetry of the Hessian gives D_x g_y=B^T, so Du=-H^{-1}B^T. Consequently grad g*=g_x(x,u) and grad F=f_x(x,u)-BH^{-1}f_y(x,u). All these quantities are continuous. (2) Continuity of v and the value derivative. For fixed lambda let q(x,y)=f_y(x,y)+lambda g_y(x,y). Its y-map is m-strongly monotone, its x-dependence is (a+lambda b)-Lipschitz, and q(x,v(x))=0. For v'=v(x'), strong monotonicity and Cauchy–Schwarz give m||v'-v(x)||<=||q(x,v')-q(x',v')||<=(a+lambda b)||x'-x||, with the zero-distance case immediate. Thus v is Lipschitz, without assuming it differentiable. Let V=L_lambda*. For a small increment h, minimization gives L_lambda(x+h,v(x+h))-L_lambda(x,v(x+h))<=V(x+h)-V(x)<=L_lambda(x+h,v(x))-L_lambda(x,v(x)). L_lambda is jointly C1 because g* is C1. Integrating its x-gradient along the x-segment, and using v(x+h)->v(x) and continuity, shows both bounds equal <grad_x L_lambda(x,v(x)),h>+o(||h||). Hence V is differentiable with this gradient; the gradient is continuous. Substituting grad g*=g_x(x,u) yields the asserted first-derivative identity. This avoids the source's chain-rule use of Dv under merely C1 assumptions on f. (3) Residual inequality, valid for arbitrary y and lambda>0. Fix x, set d=y-u, H=D_y g_y(x,u), B=D_y g_x(x,u), and define r_y=g_y(x,y)-H d and r_x=g_x(x,y)-g_x(x,u)-B d; here g_y(x,u)=0. The full Hessian bound from b-smoothness gives ||B||<=b and ||H^{-1}||<=1/mu. For either residual, integrate the corresponding Hessian block along u+t d: the k-Lipschitz Hessian gives norm <=(k/2)||d||^2, hence <=k||d||^2. Independently, the b-Lipschitz gradient and block norm <=b give norm <=2b||d||. Thus both residual norms are at most ||d|| min(2b,k||d||). Put q=grad_y L_lambda(x,y)=f_y(x,y)+lambda(Hd+r_y). Direct substitution of the formula for grad F gives the exact identity E:=grad F-grad_x L_lambda(x,y)+BH^{-1}q=f_x(x,u)-f_x(x,y)+BH^{-1}[f_y(x,y)-f_y(x,u)]+lambda[BH^{-1}r_y-r_x]. The two f-gradient differences have norms at most a||d|| each. Therefore ||E||<=(1+b/mu)||d||[a+lambda min(2b,k||d||)]. Strong convexity and b-smoothness imply b>=mu, so 1+b/mu<=2b/mu. This proves precisely the dimension-explicit Lemma A.2 bound stated in source_internal_dependency. It uses Assumption 2 for the quadratic remainder, not only Assumption 1. (4) Displacement and final constant. Set y=v, so q=0 and g_y(x,v)=-f_y(x,v)/lambda. Strong monotonicity of g_y, g_y(x,u)=0, and ||f_y(x,v)||<=c give mu||v-u||^2<=<g_y(x,v),v-u><=(c/lambda)||v-u||. Thus ||v-u||<=c/(lambda mu), including the zero case; in particular the source-used weaker bound ||v-u||<=2c/(lambda mu) holds. No unproved limiting argument or full parameter-comparison Lemma 3.2 is needed. Substituting that weaker bound into (3), using min(2b,k||v-u||)<=k||v-u|| and the value-gradient identity from (2), gives ||grad F-grad V||<=(2b/mu)(2c/(lambda mu))[a+2ck/mu]=(1/lambda)(4cb/mu^2)(a+2ck/mu). This is the exact Lemma 3.1 constant. The proof remains valid when a=0 because lambda>0 is separately required, and at lambda=2a/mu because m>=lambda mu/2 stays positive.

source_internal_dependency.statement_in_dimension_explicit_notation: For every x in X, y in R^{d_y}, lambda>0, write u=y*(x), H=D_y grad_y g(x,u) and B=D_y grad_x g(x,u). Under Assumptions 1–2, ||grad F(x)-grad_x L_lambda(x,y)+B H^{-1} grad_y L_lambda(x,y)||<=2(l_g1/mu_g)||y-u||[l_f1+lambda min(2l_g1,l_g2||y-u||)]. This is the Lemma A.2 expression with the mixed block oriented as an x-by-y matrix; the source alternates transpose conventions. The complete local argument below derives this inequality rather than treating an external lead as evidence.

assumptions: Assumption 1, PDF p.3: f is C1 with jointly l_f1-Lipschitz gradient, g is C1 with jointly l_g1-Lipschitz gradient, and ||grad_y f(x,y)||<=l_f0 for every x,y.
Assumption 2, PDF p.3: mu_g>0 and g(x,.) is mu_g-strongly convex for every x; g is C2 and its full Hessian is jointly l_g2-Lipschitz.
Constants l_f0,l_f1,l_g1,l_g2 are finite and nonnegative. The assumptions imply l_g1>=mu_g>0.

The paper also imposes standing Assumption 3: unbiased stochastic gradients of f and g with second central moments at most sigma_f^2 and sigma_g^2, respectively. No stochastic gradients are used in this analytic claim; the supplied local argument uses only Assumptions 1–2.
statement.conclusion: Both minimizers exist uniquely, and F and L_lambda* are continuously differentiable. grad L_lambda*(x)=grad_x f(x,v(x))+lambda[grad_x g(x,v(x))-grad_x g(x,u(x))]. Moreover ||grad F(x)-grad L_lambda*(x)||<=C_lambda/lambda, where C_lambda=(4l_f0 l_g1/mu_g^2)(l_f1+2l_f0 l_g2/mu_g). The paper's symbol C_lambda denotes this lambda-independent expression.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces X=R^{d_x} and Y=R^{d_y}, with positive integer dimensions. Functions f,g are real-valued on X times Y. Set u(x)=y*(x)=argmin_y g(x,y), F(x)=f(x,u(x)), g*(x)=g(x,u(x)), L_lambda(x,y)=f(x,y)+lambda(g(x,y)-g*(x)), v(x)=y_lambda*(x)=argmin_y L_lambda(x,y), and L_lambda*(x)=L_lambda(x,v(x)). All gradients are column vectors; matrix norms are induced Euclidean norms.
statement.parameter_domains: d_x,d_y positive integers; mu_g>0; finite nonnegative regularity constants; lambda>0 and lambda>=2l_f1/mu_g, including equality. No accuracy or iteration parameter is asserted.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every pair f,g satisfying these global conditions, every x in R^{d_x}, and every fixed positive lambda satisfying lambda>=2l_f1/mu_g. The conclusion is deterministic and uses exact minimizers.
